Good morning, everyone. Thank you for joining this case conference. As you know, we have a former sales executive who left last week and joined a direct competitor. We believe confidential customer information may have been used after the departure, and we may need to request a preliminary-injunction hearing within as little as three weeks. Our draft filing currently seeks broad relief covering customer information, pricing materials, and source-code documentation.

Under our pre-filing practice, I need each of you — employment counsel, forensics counsel, and insurance counsel — to report any material issues in your respective areas before I make the filing decision. Let's go through each area one at a time so I can record authorization and note any prerequisites we need completed before filing. Who would like to start?

transcript.text: I need to report a material issue. While reviewing the former executive's archived personnel file, I found a signed separation agreement containing an exclusive forum clause requiring disputes about confidential information to be filed in Illinois state court in Cook County, where the executive worked. I have not yet added this clause to the draft strategy memorandum. This could significantly affect where we file and may be a prerequisite to resolve before any filing decision is signed.

transcript.text: I have a material issue to report from the forensics side. I reviewed the access logs and forensic image this week, and I can confirm that the only company data copied to the executive's device was the customer-list database. My review did not show any copying of pricing materials or source-code documentation. I should note that I have not yet updated the evidence chart to reflect these findings. This is directly relevant to the scope of relief the draft filing currently seeks — the evidence supports claims regarding customer information, but we do not currently have forensic evidence supporting the breadth of the pricing materials and source-code documentation claims. This may need to be addressed as a prerequisite before the filing decision is signed.

transcript.text: I have a material issue to report from the insurance side. I confirmed with our broker this week that our cyber-and-crime endorsement requires the carrier's written consent before we seek injunctive relief against an employee. This confirmation is still outside the litigation file and has not yet been documented in our case materials. Given that we may seek a preliminary injunction against the former executive within three weeks, obtaining the carrier's written consent should be noted as a prerequisite before the filing decision is signed, to preserve our coverage position.

transcript.text:
Thank you all for reporting these material issues. Let me summarize what I'm hearing and what I think the implications are before I make any filing decision.

First, Thomas, the exclusive forum clause requiring disputes about confidential information to be filed in Illinois state court in Cook County is a critical issue. If that clause is binding, it could affect where we file and may prevent us from filing in our preferred forum. You need to add this clause to the draft strategy memorandum so we can fully assess its impact — I'm noting that as a prerequisite.

Second, Nadia, your forensic findings are significant. If the only data copied to the executive's device was the customer-list database, and there is no forensic evidence supporting claims regarding pricing materials or source-code documentation, then seeking broad relief on those items could expose us to challenges on the merits and potentially undermine our credibility with the court. The draft filing's scope needs to be re-examined. I'm noting that updating the evidence chart to reflect these findings is a prerequisite, and I'm inclined to narrow the injunction scope to customer information unless we develop additional evidentiary support for the other categories.

Third, Owen, the carrier's written consent requirement under the cyber-and-crime endorsement is something we need to address promptly. If we file without it, we risk jeopardizing our coverage position. I'm noting that obtaining the carrier's written consent is a prerequisite before the filing decision is signed.

So to summarize, I see three prerequisites that must be completed before I can sign the filing decision: (1) Thomas adds the exclusive forum clause to the strategy memorandum so we can determine the proper filing forum; (2) Nadia updates the evidence chart to reflect the forensic findings, and we revisit the scope of relief accordingly; and (3) Owen documents the carrier's written consent requirement in the case file and initiates the consent request.

Does anyone have anything else to add before I record my authorization decision with these stated prerequisites?
